title: Design and Modeling of the Charge Readout of a SiMOS Quantum Dot with a Single Electron Transistor and CryoCMOS
authors: Adam Quinn, Troy England, Andrew Li, Sharmila Mustari Nandita
abstract: Single electron spin qubits trapped in SiMOS quantum dots are a promising technology for scaling to thousand- or million-qubit systems due to their compatibility with mature CMOS manufacturing processes. A readout system that combines a single electron transistor with a custom cryogenic CMOS amplification and digitization chain offers key advantages by avoiding the use of bulky RF components or room-temperature interconnects. We present design techniques and simulation results for an optimized qubit-SET cryoCMOS interface, culminating in the design of the QNDR1 ASIC, the first cryogenic readout ASIC designed under the Quandarum project, which targets the development of a many-channel spin qubit based detector for use in high energy physics.
summary: This paper presents the design and simulation of QNDR1, a novel cryogenic ASIC intended to read out single electron spin qubits in SiMOS quantum dots. The authors developed advanced models for various Single Electron Transistor (SET) geometries and co-simulated them with a full CMOS readout circuit. The result is a highly integrated, low-noise readout platform crucial for scaling up solid-state quantum processors.
main_problem: The primary challenge is developing a highly scalable, low-noise, and integrated readout system for single electron spin qubits trapped in SiMOS quantum dots.
main_result: The authors designed and simulated the QNDR1 ASIC, demonstrating a functional, integrated cryogenic readout interface that achieves specified SNR and gain targets.
method: The work combines detailed device modeling (SISET, DISET, ASD) using Verilog-A with co-simulation against a custom cryogenic CMOS readout circuit (QNDR1) implemented in SpectreRF.
model_or_system: The physical system involves single electron spin qubits in SiMOS quantum dots, read out via a Single Electron Transistor (SET). The readout is integrated with a custom cryogenic CMOS amplifier and digitizer chain operating at cryogenic temperatures (3.8 K).
key_observables: Coulomb peaks, output signal voltage/current, Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR), and the Figure of Merit (FoM) for the readout circuit.
important_parameters: Operating temperature (down to 3.8 K), SET bias voltages, and the required gain (e.g., $22.5 	ext{ MV/A}$).
main_assumptions: The ASD model relies on simplifying assumptions, such as approximating the barrier region as linear; noise modeling involves combining literature estimates with analytical methods.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the objective of the Quandarum project, model fitting of SETs (SISET, DISET, ASD) to literature data, simulated Coulomb peaks for the three SET models, and the schematic/timing waveforms for the integrated SET-CMOS co-simulation setup.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the need for a scalable readout (Fig. 1), detailing the advanced modeling of SET structures (SISET, DISET, ASD) via Verilog-A, performing co-simulations with the CMOS readout, and finally presenting the full QNDR1 ASIC design, including biasing procedures and performance metrics.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the engineering bottleneck for solid-state quantum computing by providing a blueprint for integrating quantum devices with classical, low-noise cryogenic electronics.
